name: Ui_SlotTable_Pick3D
signature: u8 Ui_SlotTable_Pick3D(void* self, const RegionList3D* list)
summary: 3D hit-test over a list of axis-aligned float boxes: reads the current scene position, expands each box by half its size on every axis and returns the id byte stored at box+0x18 for the first box that contains the position, or 0.
evidence: NEW: both callers are now named (Ui_SlotTable_GetSelectedId and Ui_SlotTable_UpdateSelection), so the owner really is the UI slot table and the first pass's 'slot table' guess is confirmed; the position comes from the named Field_SceneNode_GetPosition on the overlay object.

name: Ui_SlotTable_Pick2D
signature: u8 Ui_SlotTable_Pick2D(void* self, const RegionList* list)
summary: 2D point-in-rectangle hit-test over a list of short {x, y, w, h, id} records: compares the overlay's 2D sprite position (with a two-pixel margin) against each normalised rectangle and returns the id of the first match, or 0.
evidence: NEW: callers are the named Ui_SlotTable_GetSelectedId / Ui_SlotTable_UpdateSelection. The old 'damaged' worry was a decompiler artefact only: the disassembly at 0x003DAB18..0x003DAB64 normalises both signed ranges with cmp/movle/movgt and compares them with the sprite position, then loads the id byte at [record+8]; no unrecovered register is actually used.

name: maybe_Ui_SlotTable_InitSubParts
summary: Initialises the three embedded slot-table/region parts of a UI object (constructors at self+0x5C and self+0x70 via Ui_SlotTable_UpdateSelection) and returns the address of the third part at +0xB8.
evidence: CORRECTED: the neighbour 0x003DACB0 is the UI slot-table update (Pick2D/Pick3D caller), not a casino reels routine, so 'Casino_SlotMachine' was a false friend of the word 'slot'; the caller set (Ui_SceneFlow_Update, maybe_Field_ObjectCtor) is scene-object construction, and the body is a plain three-sub-object initialiser.

name: maybe_Gfx_SceneObject_CreateFromDefs
signature: void maybe_Gfx_SceneObject_CreateFromDefs(u32 owner, void* def1, void* def2)
summary: Builds a renderable scene object from two definition blocks: copies a 5-word descriptor from def1 and a 2-word one from def2, calls the scene-node base constructor 0x002D97E8 and installs vtable 0x76D070 (then clears the state bytes).
evidence: CORRECTED: the callee 0x002D97E8 is the shared renderable mesh/scene-node constructor (14 model/mesh callers per symbols.json) and all five callers build render objects (Gfx_CollisionProxy_InitDesc, Gfx_SpriteObject_CtorWithVectors, Field_ObjectSprite_UpdatePoseRaycast, Field_ModelObj_ReleaseSprite); a message window would never sit in that call set, so the old 'Ui_MessageWindow' name was wrong. The concrete class is still unknown because vtable 0x76D070 has no named sibling.

name: maybe_Effect_ParticleEmitter_InitPoolD
summary: Allocates the 0xAC-byte effect object with vtable 0x75AFFC and a 64-entry two-word pool (ctor 0x006CEC80), falling back to the default block from 0x007261B4 when the allocation is empty. Later analysis identifies 0x75AFFC as a two-state sequence node, so the object is an effect sequence, not necessarily a particle emitter.
evidence: No new caller (none exists) and the body is the same allocate-copy-or-default template as the four 0x004C/0x004E effect-node creators; symbols.json independently calls vtable 0x75AFFC a two-state sequence class record, which confirms the effect family but not the concrete visual class, so the D suffix and maybe_ stay.

name: Battle_ApplyEquipCategoryDamageModifier
summary: Scales a battle damage value by the equipment category of the unit's slot-0 item: resolves the party member and its equipped item, reads ItemRecord+0x29 and picks one of four coefficients (f_114/f_118/f_11C, default f_120) from the data-manager record returned by 0x0063D178, then clamps the scaled value.
evidence: CORRECTED: the only caller is the named Battle_CalcActorDamageModifier, which stores the short result back into the unit record and passes it to func_00486B84; ItemRecord+0x29 is the documented equip category, so this is a battle damage coefficient chosen by equip category, not a text 'row metric' (the old name described the table offset, not the meaning).

name: maybe_Battle_Monster_GetActionRow
signature: int maybe_Battle_Monster_GetActionRow(BattleUnit* unit, void* target, int handIndex)
summary: Prepares and returns the battle message/action row for a monster actor: looks up the party-member record, the equipped item in slot 0 or 1 (handIndex), the ItemRecord+0x3B byte and the target record's +10 byte, then returns the fixed battle-work row base at +0x4238. The row-specific values are written by calls Ghidra shows without arguments.
evidence: CORRECTED: the caller Battle_RollMultiHitDamage uses this exactly where the player branch uses 'battlework+0x4238' directly, so it returns that row base, not a display-name offset; the item/target lookups are setup for the monster's row. The dropped call arguments (push {r3,...} prologue trap) keep it at maybe_.

name: maybe_Battle_Unit_RefreshDisplayValuesAlt
summary: Alternative branch of the battle-unit display refresh: converts the member's +0x73E/+0xEBE/+0xAFE display values to floats, marks the layout dirty when the enemy slot ratio changed, and pushes the pair through the message-row preset helper. The stat identity is not proven.
evidence: CORRECTED: the body is the same shape as the now-named Battle_Unit_RefreshDisplayValues (0x00496650, which reads +0x740/+0xEC0/+0xB00) but at different member offsets, and its only caller is Battle_Monster_UpdateStatBar, so it is a display-refresh variant; nothing in the body shows agility, which the old name asserted.

name: maybe_Battle_FindTargetIndexByState
summary: Resolves a target descriptor from a combatant list by state, optionally builds a target record and rolls the battle RNG (1..100) against the resolved index; returns the selected index and falls through to func_0048FE7C. Used both by action-entry building and by the AI action picker.
evidence: The two callers are now identified as action/AI code (maybe_Battle_Ui_BuildMemberActionEntries, maybe_BattleAi_PickActionByStatus) and the RNG roll plus the Battle_MonsterUi_ResolveRowType target-record build show 'find target by state' is close but incomplete; the decompiled argument registers (arg5/arg6, damaged branch) prevent a more precise name, so it stays maybe_.

name: maybe_Battle_MessageRow_RollVariance
summary: Rolls a symmetric battle-RNG value in [-f_14, f_14] and returns it together with the battle-work message-row base at +0x4238; all five callers are battle message-row builders, so this is most likely the row's random variance, not a group-attack proc roll.
evidence: CORRECTED: the caller set is entirely battle message-row code (Battle_MessageRow_BuildLayout, Text_Row_MeasureIconRowWidth, maybe_Battle_Row_SumActorValues/UpdateFromActorSlot), and the object's +0x14 is used as a symmetric range around zero; 'multi-target proc' described a use no caller supports. The return is a two-word CONCAT that Ghidra mixed up, so confidence stays low.

name: maybe_Battle_Unit_RefreshDisplayValuePair
summary: Refreshes a battle unit's alternate display values: converts the member's +0x744/+0xEC4/+0xB04 fields to floats, marks the layout dirty when the enemy slot value changed, and returns the (f_744, f_EC4) pair. Its only caller is Battle_Monster_GetMpBarRatio.
evidence: CORRECTED: the body is a third copy of the Battle_Unit_RefreshDisplayValues shape at yet another member offset block, called from the MP-bar ratio getter; the old 'GetMagicPower' name assumed a stat identity the body never reads, so the neutral display-refresh name is safer.

name: Gfx_EffectNodeCreateChild_75B1F4
summary: Virtual slot 1 of effect-node vtable 0x7785F8: allocates the 0xAC-byte child (class vtable 0x75B1F4, owner at +0x20, 64-entry two-word pool via 0x006D1990); on allocation failure it copies the default block from 0x007261B4 (f_98..f_C4) and clears f_4C.
evidence: NEW: symbols.json independently documents vtable 0x75B1F4 as a two-state effect-sequence class and names this function as the constructor that installs that class record; the four sibling creators differ only in vtable/ctor/default slice, which is exactly the allocate-copy-or-default template seen here.

name: Gfx_EffectNodeCreateChild_75B23C
summary: Virtual slot 1 of effect-node vtable 0x77C2C8: allocates the 0xAC-byte child (class vtable 0x75B23C, owner at +0x20, 64-entry two-word pool via 0x006D2004); on allocation failure it copies the default block from 0x00726074 (f_40..f_6C) and clears f_4C.
evidence: NEW: the same class-record documentation now covers 0x75B23C (two-state effect-sequence class installed by this constructor); the body is identical to 0x004CB33C except for the vtable, pool ctor and default slice, so the family and the create-child role are established.

name: maybe_Field_Actor_UpdateCameraAndAnimB
signature: u32 maybe_Field_Actor_UpdateCameraAndAnimB(FieldActor* actor, u32 arg2, int arg3)
summary: Second vfunc with the camera-projection + NPC move-animation body of 0x00591A0C: sets up the projection from the scene node, checks the actor's active flag and runs Field_NpcUpdateMoveAnimation. The damaged prologue also stores two actor fields, so it is a distinct vfunc, not a duplicate.
evidence: The prologue still reads unaff_r4/unaff_r6, so the argument list is not recovered; the named callees (Camera_SetupProjection, Field_NpcUpdateMoveAnimation, Field_SceneNode_GetPosition) only confirm the tail is the camera+move-animation update. Kept maybe_ because the decompilation is damaged.

name: maybe_Camera_FindVisiblePathEntry
summary: Searches the camera's 16-entry path table for the entry whose expanded box contains the reference point and whose path node passes the visibility chain, returning the camera work's path pointer at +0x15CC. Several halt_baddata blocks still cut the return path.
evidence: The caller is now named (maybe_Camera_UpdateFollowPosition_2) and the body uses +0x15CC, the same camera path field used by the named Camera update code, so the camera path reading is solid; the truncated control flow on the failure branches keeps it maybe_.

name: Battle_Ui_PartyPanel_PlaySe
summary: Plays the party panel's confirmation SE: picks one of the ids 0xA3F/0xA41/0xA43/0xA45 from the panel's current variant code (0x88..0x8B) and plays it through Sound_PlaySeById; in 2D mode it first checks the row object and skips when the row is empty.
evidence: NEW: the only caller is the named Battle_Ui_PartyPanel_Update and the body is a pure variant-code -> SE-id map followed by Sound_PlaySeById/Sound_GetPlayer, so both the panel ownership and the play-SE role are confirmed; the old doubt was only about the panel name.

name: Battle_Ui_PartyPanel_SpawnPartyEffect
summary: Spawns the party-panel effect for variant code 0x88..0x8D (effect ids 0x251/0x253/.../0x25B, default 0x25D) through the window's effect slot, or at the party centre when battle flag +0x4244 selects the 2D path.
evidence: NEW: the only caller is the named Battle_Ui_PartyPanel_Update and the switch maps exactly the six party variant codes to six effect ids before calling the window's spawn slot (vtable +200) and storing the handle at win+0x4C4; the party-centre fallback uses maybe_Battle_Ui_GetPartyCenter. The effect role is confirmed.

name: Battle_Ui_PartyPanel_ResetRows
summary: Rebuilds the party panel's row list: asks the panel object for its highest supported variant code (0x88..0x8F), stores it at win+0x4C7, then walks the four battle unit lists and appends every unit that accepts that code via vtable +0xE8.
evidence: NEW: the only caller is the named Battle_Ui_PartyPanel_Update; the body writes win->f_4C7 (the variant code read by PlaySe and SpawnPartyEffect) and fills win[0x1C...] from the four unit lists with the vtable +0xE8 filter, which is exactly the row-list rebuild. maybe_Ui_SelectHighestVariantCode remains the only uncertain helper.

name: maybe_Ui_TextScreen_Ctor_77E564
summary: Constructor of a screen object with a text cache: chains Ui_Screen_CtorWithTextCache, installs vtable 0x77E564, sets the -1/0 defaults at +0xC98/+0xC99, initialises the text-line cache at +0xCA4 and clears the six-word block and two flag bytes before it.
evidence: The requesting factory is now named Field_ObjectFactory_Kind14, but it does not identify the concrete screen; the ctor shape and the named callees (Ui_Screen_CtorWithTextCache, Ui_TextLineCache_InitAndReturn, FieldParty_ResetMemberSlot) confirm the text-cache screen but not which one, so maybe_ stays.

name: maybe_Effect_SpawnOrientedInstance
summary: Spawns an effect instance from a request carrying a locator/actor reference and a direction: derives an orthonormal basis from the source transform, fills the 0xE0-byte parameter block and calls Effect_FindOrCreateInstance with the resulting matrix.
evidence: This is a recovered entry point with no direct callers (checked again); the basis maths and the final Effect_FindOrCreateInstance call are clear, and the request struct layout is only positional, so the name remains a maybe_.

name: Party_GetMemberCount
summary: Counts the used party-member slots by walking the id bytes at self+0x944C until the 0xFF terminator; returns 8 for an empty table. The decompiler cut the counting loop into a noreturn wcslen call, but the byte scan is visible.
evidence: NEW: five of the six callers are now named (Ui_PartyList_InsertMember, Ui_ShopItemInfo_FillStats, Menu_StatusScreen_InitFaceAndCommands, Party_GetMemberRecord, Party_HasFreeMemberSlot), all of which need the member count before indexing the party tables; the only helper is the mis-marked wcslen, which only truncates the decompiled loop.

name: maybe_Item_IsAnyRequiredItemElsewhere
signature: u32 maybe_Item_IsAnyRequiredItemElsewhere(u32 self, RecipeRow* row, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Menu-condition test over a record's four required item ids: for each non-0xFFFF id, if a storage instance exists but the default-storage lookup resolves to a different instance, return 1. It is the 'is any required material held somewhere other than the normal item storage' check.
evidence: NEW: the single caller is now named Ui_MenuCondition_Evaluate, and it calls this in the 'kind 0' branch with a condition record, which matches the four-id row layout; the exact meaning of 'Item_GetStoragePointer != Item_CountEquipped(kind, id)' still rests on the callee names, so maybe_ stays.

name: maybe_Item_AreRequiredItemsOwned
signature: u32 maybe_Item_AreRequiredItemsOwned(u32 self, RecipeRow* row, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Alternative ownership test over the same four-id row: when the selector at +0x1A is -1 every non-empty material id must pass the kind-filtered presence test (Item_CountEquipped), otherwise the selector must equal the value returned by 0x0023D078(kind,0).
evidence: The record layout matches the condition record handled by 0x006301A4 (same +0x11 kind and +0x12/+0x14/+0x16/+0x18 ids), but the decompiled body returns 0 on the innermost success path, so the polarity is untrustworthy; the listed 'Uma' callers are data/vtable references, not direct calls, so the pair with 0x006301A4 is the strongest evidence and maybe_ stays.

name: maybe_Field_FindNpcBalloonEntryAlt
signature: BalloonEntry* maybe_Field_FindNpcBalloonEntryAlt(u32 table, u32 field, u32 arg3, u32 scratch)
summary: Second instantiation of the NPC balloon-entry search: resolves the NPC entry, maps its quest state (func_0066AF08) to a balloon type byte 3/6/... and returns the balloon record; falls back to the entry's own +0x14 pointer when the NPC has no quest state.
evidence: Only caller is now named (maybe_Ui_TrainingWindow_SelectTitleRow), but the decode still uses unaff_r6-style registers in the argument list, so the parameter order and the 'Alt' distinction cannot be verified; kept maybe_.

name: std_FormatSinkPutNarrow
signature: void std_FormatSinkPutNarrow(void* sink, const u16* src, int count)
summary: Copies a UTF-16 run into a narrow printf sink: converts each unit through the locale codec, stops at the terminator or the sink's hard limit, and when the width budget would be exceeded flushes, pads with PadZero/PadSpace, emits the already-converted bytes through the callback at sink+4 and charges the budget.
evidence: NEW: the caller is the named std_FormatSinkPutString and the pad helpers are named std_Format_PadZero/PadSpace, so this is unambiguously the narrow-character branch of the std printf sink family; the codec call is the only unnamed callee.

name: Mem_PoolDestroy
signature: void Mem_PoolDestroy(Pool* pool, u32 block, u32 count, u32 flags)
summary: Empties a pool: walks its four sublists, detaches every chunk through the chunk callback 0x0011B034, then re-initialises the pool descriptor and marks it reset (f_86=1).
evidence: NEW: the caller set is now named (Sound_StreamBuffer_Dtor, Sound_StreamPlayer_Release, Snd_StopVoiceByHandle, Fs_SubmitAsyncTransfer) and the callees are the named Mem_PoolInit/Container_ListAppend, so 'empty and re-init a pool' is confirmed; the three trailing parameters are unused by the recovered body, hence the reconstructed prototype.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_AdvanceChildAndSetCharacter
summary: Window virtual that advances the active child page (self+4 +0x748), pushes the pane pair at +0x13C/+0xBFC with the shared layout descriptor, then applies the page's current member id to the status panel at +0xB5C.
evidence: The body is byte-identical to 0x003F0CEC, which is vtable slot 0 of UiJumonWindow (0x76B9B4) and is now confirmed under that class; this copy has no caller or vtable owner, so the effect is clear but the owning class is not - kept maybe_ with the neutral window name.

name: Ui_JumonWindow_AdvanceChildAndSetCharacter
summary: Command handler of the spell (jumon) window: advances the active child page, pushes the spell pane with the shared layout descriptor and applies the page's current member to the status panel.
evidence: NEW: this is vtable slot 0 of the UiJumonWindow class table 0x76B9B4 and all four callees are named (Ui_Window_AdvanceActiveChild, Ui_JumonWindow_PushPane, Party_GetMemberIdAtCurrentPage, Ui_StatusPanel_SetCharacter); the earlier doubt was only the word 'ExecCommand', which this name replaces with what the body does.

name: maybe_Ui_ItemScreen_NextStep
signature: void maybe_Ui_ItemScreen_NextStep(u32* outPair, UiStateMachine* sm, u32 arg3)
summary: Chooses the next item-screen step: if the page text scroll is unfinished it selects command 10, otherwise command 9 plus one advance of the row list, then returns the matching handler pair from the 0x00729554 table.
evidence: The body is a handler-table slot with no direct caller; the callees are named (Ui_TextScroll_IsFinished, Ui_Window_AdvanceActiveChild, Ui_ActivateScreenMessageAndModel) and the pair comes from 0x00729554, but neither the item-screen ownership nor the step semantics is proven, so maybe_ stays.

name: maybe_Ui_State_SetState24
summary: State entry of the same state machine as 0x001C0DE4: fills the transition record with invalid defaults, advances the active child of the manager at +0x1E7C, sets state index 0x18 and copies the two-word target out of 0x007295C0+4.
evidence: NEW: 0x007295C0 is the table cited by the named Ui_ShopItemList_HandleInput/MoveCursor/BeginBuy, so this entry belongs to the shop item-list family; it is called from Ui_Window_RegisterEventContext and maybe_Ui_State_HandleEvent, which keeps open whether it is generic state-machine code or shop-only.

name: maybe_Ui_ItemIcon_PlaceInLine
signature: void maybe_Ui_ItemIcon_PlaceInLine(TextLine* line, u32 itemId, u32 column, int glyphSlot)
summary: Places an inline item icon into a text line: when glyphSlot is negative it looks the item up and, if the id is equipment (0xA4..0x9BF or 0xB19..0xB1C), resolves its icon category with func_0066C724 and writes it into the line at column; otherwise it maps the equipment slot through the party member's record before writing.
evidence: CORRECTED: the parameters are a text line plus column/glyph slot, and the body writes through func_002F6ACC on the line object, so 'PlaceItemInMemberSlot' described the lookup, not the operation. The body does resolve item rows, so this is item-icon placement code (not a text-measurement function); the exact line API is unnamed, hence maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_ItemScreen_CloseList
summary: Closes the item-list sub-view: resets the list, reads the selected member id from the list cursor and chains to Ui_TextScroll_End, then stores the two handler words from the 0x00729554 table.
evidence: The callees are named (Ui_ListCursor_GetSelectedMemberId, Ui_TextScroll_End) and the handler pair comes from 0x00729554, which supports the close/select reading; there is still no caller or vtable slot tying it to the item screen, so maybe_ stays.

name: maybe_Ui_ItemScreen_HandleCursorInput
summary: Handles the item screen's input bits: on bit 1 it forwards the cursor triple, on bits 0x102 it recomputes the cursor offset from the row/page size and selects the entry, and on bit 4 it resets the cursor to 0xFF.
evidence: CORRECTED: the body reads the input flags from Text_InvokeControlHandler and dispatches three distinct actions, so 'ToggleCursor' covered only one branch; the callees are named but the item-screen ownership is still assumed from the shared 0x729554 handler family, so maybe_ stays.

name: Ui_Widget_SetupAnimTransition
signature: void Ui_Widget_SetupAnimTransition(UiWidget* widget, uint32_t animId, int mode)
summary: Pushes the widget's animation pane and sets two animation values: maps animId through func_002BBAD0 and stores it in the animation block at widget+0x13C/+0xCC0, then optionally maps and stores mode as the second value.
evidence: NEW: all eleven callers are UI screens/panels (Ui_StatusPanel_ChangeMember, Battle_StatusIcon_Update, Field_Menu_OpenJumonWindow, ...) and the callee Ui_JumonWindow_PushPane is named, so this is a UI widget animation setup, not the old model transition; the two id-mapping helpers remain unnamed, hence 0.5 rather than higher.

name: Field_GetCurrentRoomId
summary: Twin of Field_GetCurrentPlaceId (0x001D607C): returns 0 unless a map is loaded, otherwise the f_11 byte of the scene record from 0x0066A7D8, i.e. the room id next to the place id at f_12.
evidence: NEW: the sibling 0x001D607C is now confidently named Field_GetCurrentPlaceId and reads f_12; this copy is otherwise identical and reads f_11, and its callers are the named Field_Menu_OpenJumonWindow and maybe_Ui_FieldMessageWindow_Init, which need the current room. The place/room assignment of the two bytes is consistent but still inferred.

name: Camera_UpdateScreenViews
summary: Per-frame camera view update: when the current camera work is idle and the flag byte at +0x11 is set, it optionally refreshes the follow position, then resets and updates the two screen-view slots at +0x54 (+0x15CC stride 0x2AF*4) and finally calls the shared screen-view updater.
evidence: CORRECTED: 'TryStartWork' missed that the body always resets and updates both screen-view objects after the idle gate; the caller is the named Ui_SceneFlow_Update, the callee set is Gfx_ScreenView_ResetAll/UpdateAll, and the +0x15CC/+0x15DC fields are the same camera work fields used by the named camera path code, so this is the camera's per-frame screen-view update.

name: Battle_Popup_Dtor
summary: Destructor of a battle popup object: releases +0x1D4, re-splices three intrusive list heads, destroys the 0x60 container, installs two sub-object vtables, destroys two 0x24-byte arrays and the list node at -0x174, then frees.
evidence: CORRECTED: eleven of the twelve callers are the named Battle_Popup_Ensure* functions (MissSingle, Heal, Crit, Damage, MpDamage, LargePerSlot, MissCombo), so this is the shared popup teardown, not a generic 'Ui_LargeWindow'; the body is the reverse-order teardown template with the final delete helper 0x0010F6CC.

name: maybe_Ui_Screen_Dtor
summary: Deleting destructor of a large UI screen: stamps the vtable, releases the embedded layout references and animation lists, destroys the 0x5C/0xFC/0x3B8/0x9C member arrays, tears down four embedded sub-objects (including 0x0036813C) and the base object.
evidence: CORRECTED: the old 'Ctor' label was wrong - the body only releases/destroys (Ui_LayoutRef_Release, std_destroy_range, Ui_Object_DtorBase) and never allocates, and it calls the 0x0036813C member teardown; it has no caller or vtable sibling, so the 'Screen' class label is still inferred, hence maybe_ at 0.4.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_DtorDeep
summary: Destructor of a window with a deep embedded chain: releases the pane chain at self+0x230, the sub-object at +0x1E0, destroys the 0x5C-stride array and frees.
evidence: No named caller or vtable sibling; the teardown idiom and the 0x5C-stride array are verified but nothing identifies the class, so the maybe_ name and confidence stay.

name: maybe_Ui_Screen_DtorDelete_2
summary: Deleting destructor of a large screen object: destroys the 0x9C-stride sub-widget array (0x23 entries), the nested widget at -0x1684 and frees the screen.
evidence: Only self-references; the 0x9C/0x23 layout and the teardown order are consistent with a screen but no named ctor or vtable sibling confirms the class, so maybe_ stays.

name: maybe_Ui_TitleWindow_Dtor
summary: Destructor of a small window object: detaches the child sprite, removes the node from its owner's ring, releases the tween/layout members and frees.
evidence: No named ctor or vtable sibling references a title window; the teardown mechanism matches the other deleting dtors in this batch but the class label is unverified, so maybe_ stays.

name: maybe_Ui_CursorIcon_DtorB
summary: Non-deleting destructor of a small UI sub-object: stamps vtable 0x75A3E4, destroys the intrusive child ring and the embedded layout references, and returns the enclosing pointer without freeing.
evidence: NEW: five named callers now exist (Ui_TimeWindow_Dtor calls it on a sub-object at -0xC0, plus Menu_Senreki/MonsterList/PresentPanel setup paths), which confirms it is a reusable sub-object dtor; the class label 'CursorIcon' still comes only from the first pass, and vtable 0x75A3E4 has no named sibling, so maybe_ stays.

name: maybe_Ui_DetachMembers
summary: In-place reset of an embedded UI object: stores the new vtable/handler word at +0x18, destroys the 0x50-byte pane at +0x64 and the list at +0x18, and returns the enclosing object pointer.
evidence: NEW: the eight callers are setup/update paths (Ui_SmithMenu_StepOptionIndex, Ui_SubWindow_UpdateValueText, Ui_TxtLowerWindow_InitPanes, Ui_ThreeLineTwoSelectWindow_InitLayout, Ui_TalkWindow_SetText, Ui_DiveWindow_CyclePage, Ui_Message_SetArgsFromRecord...), so this is a reset that tears down the old embedded sub-object before reuse; 'DetachMembers' is still a guess about the semantic, kept maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_EquipWindow_Dtor
summary: Deleting destructor of an equipment-window sub-object: stores the owner back-pointer at +0x4C, performs five relative Ui_LayoutRef_Release steps, installs the two nested vtables, destroys the list and frees.
evidence: There is already a confident Ui_EquipWindow_Dtor at 0x003357F4, so this cannot be the window itself; the adjacent pair (with 0x003332C0) is a deleting/non-deleting dtor of an embedded member, and the equip-window family comes only from the 'win_equip_*' panes, hence maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_EquipWindow_DtorBase
summary: Non-deleting destructor twin of 0x00333240 for the same embedded equipment-window sub-object (identical body without the final free).
evidence: Same body as 0x00333240 without the free call, so the pair is a D0/D2-style split; the owning equip-window class is still inferred from the neighbouring panes, so maybe_ stays.

name: maybe_Ui_GuideWindow_Dtor
summary: Deleting destructor of a small embedded UI sub-object: stamps its vtable, releases the 0x50-byte pane at +0x4C and the list, then frees. Same four-line template as 0x00383724/0x00398B7C.
evidence: NEW: the only caller is now named maybe_Ui_Screen_Dtor (0x004119E0), which tears down this member inside the large screen, so the 'member dtor' role is confirmed; the concrete 'GuideWindow' class label is still not proven by a ctor or vtable sibling, so maybe_ stays.

name: maybe_Ui_GuideWindow_DtorBase
summary: Non-deleting destructor twin of 0x0036813C for the same embedded sub-object (same body without the free).
evidence: Same four-line body as 0x0036813C minus func_0010F6CC; the pair is a deleting/non-deleting split and the class label remains the first pass's inference, so maybe_ stays.

name: maybe_Ui_IconText_Dtor
summary: Deleting destructor of a small embedded UI widget: stamps its vtable, releases the pane at +0x4C and the list, then frees (same template as 0x0036813C).
evidence: NEW: the only caller is the named Ui_SakusenWindow_Dtor, so this is a member destructor of the Sakusen window; the 'IconText' class label is still an unverified first-pass inference, hence maybe_.
